WhyInopi.title: Learning innovation is growing across Indonesia, but it is not yet connected
WhyInopi.body: Learning innovation in Indonesia comes from universities, schools, industry, and government. Most of it, however, happens in isolation: research stays in journals, technology does not reach the classroom, and industry needs go unheard by educators. INOPI connects all of them in one ecosystem, so ideas can be tested, applied, and turned into real impact.

logo.title: The Meaning of Our Logo
logo.intro: The INOPI logo is minimalist, built from simple geometric forms.

items.title: The diamond
items.desc: Stands for balance, precision, and integrity. Its four sides represent four pillars of learning that support one another as equals: educators, learners, institutions, and innovation. Its shape also resembles a gemstone, a symbol of knowledge that is continually refined.

items.title: The diagonal line
items.desc: Represents the flow of ideas and the shift from conventional to innovative practice, bridging theory and practice. It also forms an implied letter "I": Innovation and Indonesia.

items.title: The small circle at the top
items.desc: Represents ideas and sparks of insight. Placed outside the main shape, it signals openness to new thinking. It also resembles a human head: the learner at the center of everything the association does.

items.title: The neutral palette
items.desc: Taupe and warm brown convey wisdom, depth, stability, and sustainability.

points.title: Mass AI Adoption, Lagging Workforce Readiness
points.desc: Companies and educational institutions are adopting AI quickly, but workforce competency has not caught up. The need for structured training is very large and has not been served systematically. The association needs to step in to fill this gap as a provider of standards and competency development.

points.title: The Association's Launch Needs a Flagship Program
points.desc: The launch momentum is effective only when accompanied by a real program, not just a declaration. Training is the fastest program to execute and the one whose benefits members feel immediately. It marks INOPI's identity and credibility from day one.

rationale.conclusion: Training is the first concrete step — immediate impact, fast to execute, and INOPI's flagship program at launch.

rights.title: Member rights
rights.body: attend and speak at the General Assembly of Members; vote and stand for election in accordance with the Articles of Association and Bylaws; receive INOPI services, guidance, and information; propose programs; and receive the board's accountability reports.

duties.title: Member responsibilities
duties.body: comply with the Articles of Association, Bylaws, and INOPI's code of ethics; take an active part in activities; uphold INOPI's reputation; pay the registration fee and annual membership fee; and provide accurate information and report any changes to member data.

faqs.q: What membership categories does INOPI offer?
faqs.a: There are three categories: Student for university and school students, Professional for lecturers and practitioners, and Corporate for companies and institutions, with a quota of three people.

faqs.q: What are Molen and NEXT EDU?
faqs.a: Molen is a national-scale monthly online learning event held every month. NEXT EDU is INOPI's annual gathering, or summit. Both are open to all membership categories.
You can apply through the form on this site, or in person at {eyebrow}, {dateLabel} at {venue}.
In addition to all core benefits, Corporate members receive special rates on EdTech services from fellow members, EdTech lab consultation by PPOTD, and the annual industry outlook.

faqs.q: How do I pay the membership fee?
faqs.a: Payment information is sent by email after your application has been verified.

Privacy.title: INOPI Privacy Policy

sections.title: 1. Who we are
sections.body: This website is operated by Perkumpulan Asosiasi Inovasi Pembelajaran Indonesia (INOPI). INOPI is responsible for the personal data collected through this website.

sections.title: 2. Data we collect
sections.intro: We only collect data you provide directly through our forms:
items: Membership form: name, email, WhatsApp number, institution, position, areas of interest, and membership category.
Partnership form: name, email, phone number (optional), organization, and collaboration details.
Contact form: name, email, topic, and message.
sections.outro: We may also collect anonymous website usage data (such as pages visited) to understand how the website is used. This data is not used to identify you personally.

sections.title: 3. How we use your data
items: To process membership applications and fees.
To follow up on partnership proposals and enquiries.
To send information about INOPI activities, only if you have agreed to receive it.
To improve our website and services.

sections.title: 4. Who can access your data
sections.body: Data is accessed only by INOPI board members responsible for handling the relevant request. We do not sell your personal data. We may use technology service providers (such as email and hosting services) that are bound to keep the data confidential.

sections.title: 5. Storage and security
sections.body: Data is stored with restricted access and reasonable technical safeguards, for as long as needed for the purposes above.

sections.title: 6. Your rights
sections.body: You may request access to, correction of, or deletion of your personal data, and withdraw your consent to receive activity information at any time. This policy follows the principles of Indonesia's Law No. 27 of 2022 on Personal Data Protection.

sections.title: 7. Contact us
sections.body: Send requests regarding your personal data to asosiasi.inopi@gmail.com with the subject "Personal Data".

sections.title: 8. Changes to this policy
sections.body: This policy may be updated. The latest version is always available on this page.

Privacy.note: This is an English translation. If there is any difference between the English and Bahasa Indonesia versions, the Bahasa Indonesia version prevails.
